history.summary: IMPORTANT: THIS IS NOT A TEMPLE. There is no 'Nongkrem Dance Festival Temple' - the CSV name conflates two different things, and the CSV town 'Mairang' is also wrong (Mairang is in Eastern West Khasi Hills, ~40 km from Shillong). What exists is the Ka Pomblang Nongkrem (Nongkrem Dance / Shad Nongkrem), a five-day religious festival of the Khasi people held annually in November at Smit, the traditional seat of Hima Khyrim in East Khasi Hills, ~11-15 km from Shillong - Nongkrem is the namesake Khasi village and former venue, Smit the present one. The festival is part of the pom-blang (goat-killing) ceremony: the Syiem (chieftain) of Khyrim, aided by the soh-blei (high priest) and lyngdohs, sacrifices a goat (sometimes preceded by a cock) to Ka Blei Synshar, the ruling goddess, and to the deity of Shillong Peak and the ruling clan's ancestors, praying for a good harvest and the prosperity of the Hima. On the fourth day the dance unfolds at the sacred grounds of Lum Pomblang and Madan Syiem, adjoining the Syiem's historic thatched wooden palace (Iing Sad): unmarried maidens in silk and gold/silver ornaments perform Ka Shad Kynthei in the inner circle while young men in traditional regalia perform the vigorous Ka Shad Mastieh with swords (waitlam) and yak-hair whisks (symphiah) in the outer circle, to drums and tangmuri pipes. NOTE ON 'WEIKING': the Weiking ground in Shillong is the venue of the separate Ka Shad Suk Mynsiem spring festival (April, organised by Seng Khasi), not of Ka Pomblang Nongkrem - the two festivals are often confused. The Meghalaya government has recently developed visitor infrastructure at the Smit grounds (Lum Pomblang and Madan Syiem) to promote cultural tourism. The dataset owner should decide whether to retain this record as a 'temple' entry or reclassify it as a sacred/festival site.

name: Nongkrem Dance Festival Temple
town_description: Smit is the traditional capital of Hima Khyrim, one of the principal Khasi states, in East Khasi Hills district, about 11-15 km from Shillong. It is the seat of the Syiem (chieftain) of Khyrim, whose historic thatched wooden palace (Iing Sad) stands at the heart of the village, and the venue of the annual Ka Pomblang Nongkrem festival at the sacred grounds of Lum Pomblang and Madan Syiem. The namesake village of Nongkrem lies nearby in the same hills.

travel.airport: Shillong (Umroi) Airport, approx. 30-40 km (verify), has limited scheduled services (verify); the nearest major airport is Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati, Assam (approx. 100-120 km by road; verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati railway station is the nearest major railhead (approx. 100-120 km by road; verify); onward by taxi or bus to Shillong and Smit.
travel.road: Smit is approx. 11-15 km from Shillong, reachable by taxi and local buses; the festival grounds (Lum Pomblang, Madan Syiem) adjoin the Syiem's palace at Smit.

visitor_information.best_time: November, during the five-day Ka Pomblang Nongkrem festival (exact dates vary yearly; check with Meghalaya Tourism). October-March otherwise for pleasant hill weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not applicable - this is an open festival ground, not a temple with daily hours (verify). The sacred rites (Pomblang sacrifice) are restricted ceremonies; visitors should attend respectfully, dress modestly, and follow local custom - photography of rituals may be restricted (verify).
